author: Declaration Desk
title: India extends $500 million credit line to Guyana as Jaishankar meets leaders at Commonwealth summit
dek: The External Affairs Minister also met the Australian and British prime ministers at CHOGM in Antigua and Barbuda.
body:
India has extended a $500 million line of credit to Guyana for roads, health and defence projects, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said after meeting Guyana's President Irfaan Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda.

"Announced extention of USD 500 mn Line of Credit for roads, health & defence projects," Mr Jaishankar wrote on X, adding that the two sides had reviewed progress in cooperation since Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Guyana in November 2024. Agreements were signed on supplying and installing equipment for small manufacturing projects and on grants for quick-impact community projects, and the two sides discussed India's help in building digital public infrastructure, including a UPI-like payments system, in Guyana, ANI reported. The terms of the credit line were not published.

Guyana, home to a large Indian-origin community, has become one of the world's fastest-growing oil producers since output began in 2019.

Mr Jaishankar, who represented India at the summit, also met Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. With Mr Burnham he discussed "strengthening our economic partnership in the context of CETA", the India-UK trade agreement that recently came into force, he wrote. CHOGM, held from 1 to 4 November under the theme "Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth", brings together the 56 Commonwealth members, of which India is the largest by population.
